change_note: Cards for the nine iShares funds, from each fund's official page, re-checked by a second reader.
how_to_read: Each card says in plain words what the fund holds and which index it follows.
The yearly cost is the share of the money in the fund that it keeps each year to run itself; lower is better.
A fund card describes the fund. It is not a forecast and not a reason to buy or sell.

funds.name: iShares Core S&P 500 ETF
funds.holds: Shares of about five hundred large US companies chosen by S&P, each weighted by its market size, so the largest tech firms carry the most weight.
funds.plain: A low-cost way to own a slice of the big US companies that make up the best-known US stock market index.
funds.top_note: Tilted to technology: as of Oct 8, 2026 the tech sector was about 40% of the fund and the top ten holdings about 39%, led by NVIDIA, Apple and Microsoft.

funds.name: iShares MSCI ACWI ETF
funds.holds: Large and mid-sized companies from both rich and emerging countries around the world, weighted by market size; the US makes up most of it.
funds.plain: One fund that spreads money across stock markets all over the world, in both developed and emerging countries.
funds.top_note: Despite the global label, the United States was about 65% of the fund as of Oct 8, 2026, and technology about a third.

funds.name: iShares MSCI EAFE ETF
funds.holds: Large and mid-sized companies in developed countries outside the US and Canada, led by Japan, Britain, France, Switzerland and Germany.
funds.plain: A way to own big companies in rich countries other than the US and Canada, to spread money beyond the American market.
funds.top_note: Japan was the largest country at about 25% as of Oct 8, 2026, followed by the United Kingdom at about 14%. The fund is exposed to currency moves against the dollar.

funds.name: iShares Core MSCI Emerging Markets ETF
funds.holds: Large, mid-sized and small companies in emerging-market countries such as Taiwan, South Korea, China, India and Brazil.
funds.plain: A low-cost way to own a broad mix of companies in developing economies, from big names down to smaller firms.
funds.index_tracked: MSCI Emerging Markets Investable Market Index (USD) (Net)
funds.top_note: Concentrated in Asian chipmakers: Taiwan Semiconductor alone was about 14% of the fund as of Oct 8, 2026, and Taiwan plus South Korea together were about half.

funds.name: iShares MSCI Israel ETF
funds.holds: Israeli company shares of all sizes, with banks and other financial firms the largest group, followed by technology, health care and industrial firms.
funds.plain: A single fund for owning a broad set of Israeli companies, most of them traded on the Tel Aviv stock exchange.
funds.index_tracked: MSCI Israel Capped Investable Market Index (Net)
funds.top_note: Concentrated: the top ten holdings were about 55% as of Oct 8, 2026, led by Teva at about 11%, with Bank Leumi and Bank Hapoalim next. Financials were about 35%.

funds.name: iShares Core S&P Small-Cap ETF
funds.holds: Shares of several hundred smaller US companies chosen by S&P, weighted by market size; since all are small, no single company is a big part of the fund.
funds.plain: A low-cost way to own many smaller US companies, which can behave differently from the giants that dominate the main index.
funds.top_note: Widely spread: no single holding was much above half a percent of the fund as of Oct 8, 2026.

funds.name: iShares Semiconductor ETF
funds.holds: About thirty US-listed chip companies, some of them based abroad, that design or make computer chips or the machines used to make them.
funds.plain: A way to own the chip industry as a whole instead of a single chip company; it rises and falls with that one industry.
funds.top_note: Narrow and concentrated: about thirty stocks, with the top ten about 61% as of Oct 8, 2026, led by AMD, Intel, Micron, NVIDIA and Broadcom. iShares lists a planned share split with a record date of Nov 3, 2026.

funds.name: iShares Core U.S. Aggregate Bond ETF
funds.holds: Thousands of investment-grade bonds priced in US dollars, mostly US Treasury bonds, home-mortgage bonds and bonds from large companies.
funds.plain: A low-cost way to own the broad US investment-grade bond market in one fund.
funds.top_note: About 47% Treasuries and 23% mortgage pass-through bonds as of Oct 8, 2026. Effective duration is about 5.7 years, so the fund's value falls when interest rates rise.

funds.name: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF
funds.holds: US government Treasury bonds that have more than twenty years left before they are paid back.
funds.plain: A way to own long-dated US government bonds, whose value moves a lot when interest rates change.
funds.index_tracked: ICE US Treasury 20+ Year Bond Index
funds.top_note: Very sensitive to interest rates: effective duration was about 14.7 years as of Oct 8, 2026, across about 47 bond issues.
